extraction.name: LAMBADA
extraction.description: LAMBADA is a collection of narrative passages where human subjects can guess the last word when exposed to the whole passage but not when only seeing the last sentence. It evaluates computational models' ability to understand broad discourse context through a word prediction task.
extraction.creator: Denis Papemo, Germán Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bemardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, Raquel Fernández
extraction.publisher: CIMeC - Center for Mind/Brain Sciences, University of Trento
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from the BookCorpus (unpublished novels), filtered for duplicates and offensive material, divided into training and dev+test partitions by novel, filtered to remove passages easy for standard language models, and then evaluated by human subjects via CrowdFlower crowdsourcing in three steps.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The BookCorpus, containing unpublished novels; after duplicate removal and filtering, it contains 5,325 novels and 465 million words.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Multi-step crowdsourcing pipeline: (1) one subject guesses target word from full passage; if correct, (2) a second subject guesses from full passage; if correct, (3) up to 10 subjects try to guess from target sentence only (3 guesses each); passage included in dataset only if no subject in step 3 guesses correctly. Subjects paid $0.22/page in steps 1-2 and $0.15/page in step 3.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: 84–86% of items were discarded at step 1, an additional 6–7% at step 2, and another 3–5% at step 3. Only about 1 in 25 input examples passed all selection steps. Average cost per retained item was $1.24.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: At least 2 annotators for passage-level guessing (steps 1-2), plus up to 10 annotators for sentence-only guessing (step 3)
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is derived from unpublished novels in the BookCorpus, which minimizes the usefulness of general world knowledge and external resources. The corpus was filtered for potentially offensive material using a stop word list, and duplicate removal was applied.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for evaluating language understanding in NLP models, specifically the ability to predict a target word given a broader discourse context. Models tackling LAMBADA should be trained on raw text from the training partition.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Novels were randomly divided into equally-sized training and development+testing partitions; LAMBADA dataset was built from the latter partition with 4,869 development and 5,153 test passages from 1,331 and 1,332 disjoint novels respectively.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Duplicate removal and filtering of potentially offensive material using a stop word list; context size defined as minimum number of complete sentences cumulatively containing at least 50 tokens before the target sentence; target word constrained to be the last word of the target sentence.

name.evidence: We introduce LAMBADA, a dataset to evaluate the capabilities of computational models for text understanding by means of a word prediction task.

description.evidence: LAMBADA is a collection of narrative passages sharing the characteristic that human subjects are able to guess their last word if they are exposed to the whole passage, but not if they only see the last sentence preceding the target word.
